Assertion: SRA accepts raw or minimally processed sequence reads, not assembled contigs.
Raw read archives require per-base quality information; FASTA alone is insufficient.
Study/BioProject, Sample/BioSample, Experiment and Run are distinct linked objects.
Paired files from one library belong to one Run; different samples are not grouped into one Run.
A submission tracking ID such as SUB is not the accession cited in a paper.
Human metagenomes require consent, access and host-sequence review before release.
A read submission requires pre-registered study and sample records plus experiment/library metadata.
A primary metagenome assembly should be linked to its raw runs.
A MAG uses a derived sample record and should retain links to lower-level reads and assemblies.
Webin-CLI validation and submission are separate operations.
Internal submission identifiers are not the final public sequence accessions.
A Git branch or mutable tag is not a preservation DOI.
A new Zenodo version has new files and a version-specific persistent identifier linked to prior versions.
CITATION.cff exposes preferred citation metadata but does not itself preserve a release.
An image tag is mutable while a digest identifies content.
A multi-platform index digest and a platform manifest digest identify different objects.
A reproducible database record needs release, artifact, checksum and source, not a database name alone.
A Data Availability statement covers both generated and reused data and gives persistent identifiers or restrictions.
Code availability is recorded separately from scientific data availability.
FAIR does not require sensitive human files to be openly downloadable; metadata and access procedures can be public.
Existing public tutorial data must be cited and reused, not resubmitted as a new investigator-owned study.
Derived tables, catalogs, MAGs and UViGs must point back to samples/runs and analysis versions.
